welcome.text: Hello, little explorer! Let us discover something new.

try-again.text: Good try! Let us listen again.

question-5-6-ant.text: It is a tiny insect with bent antennae and a narrow waist that often walks in a line.

question-5-6-apple.text: It is a round red fruit.

question-5-6-banana.text: It is a long, curved yellow fruit.

question-5-6-bat.text: It is a furry mammal with wings made of thin skin.

question-5-6-bear.text: It is a large bear with brown fur, round ears, and big paws.

question-5-6-beaver.text: It has big front teeth and a wide, flat tail shaped like a paddle.

question-5-6-bee.text: It is a fuzzy, buzzing insect with yellow-and-dark stripes that visits flowers.

question-5-6-blue.text: It is the color of a clear daytime sky.

question-5-6-butterfly.text: It is an insect with four large, colorful wings and a thin body.

question-5-6-camel.text: It has long legs and humps on its back, and can travel through deserts.

question-5-6-car.text: It has four wheels and carries people.

question-5-6-cat.text: It is a little pet that says meow.

question-5-6-circle.text: It is round, with no corners.

question-5-6-crab.text: It has a wide hard shell, ten legs, and two claws at the front.

question-5-6-crocodile.text: It is a long, scaly reptile with a powerful tail and a long, toothy snout.

question-5-6-deer.text: It is a slim, hoofed animal; the one in our picture has branching antlers.

question-5-6-dog.text: It is a pet that says woof.

question-5-6-dolphin.text: It is a sleek sea mammal with a beak-like snout and a curved mouth.

question-5-6-dragon.text: It is a Chinese mythical creature with a long, winding body, horns, and claws.

question-5-6-duck.text: It is a water bird with a broad, flat bill that says quack.

question-5-6-eagle.text: The bird in our picture has a white head, broad brown wings, and a hooked yellow beak.

question-5-6-elephant.text: It is a huge animal with a long trunk.

question-5-6-flamingo.text: It is a pink bird with very long legs and a curved neck.

question-5-6-flower.text: It has colorful petals and a stem.

question-5-6-fox.text: It has pointed ears, orange fur, and a bushy tail with a white tip.

question-5-6-frog.text: It has smooth, moist skin and long back legs for jumping near ponds.

question-5-6-giraffe.text: It has a very long neck and a coat covered in brown patches.

question-5-6-goat.text: It is a farm animal that often has a beard and curved horns.

question-5-6-goose.text: It is a long-necked water bird that honks; our picture shows white feathers.

question-5-6-gorilla.text: It is a large, dark-furred ape with a broad chest and no tail.

question-5-6-grapes.text: These small purple fruits grow in a bunch.

question-5-6-green.text: It is the color of fresh grass.

question-5-6-heart.text: It has two rounded bumps and a point at the bottom.

question-5-6-hedgehog.text: It is a small mammal with a back covered in short, sharp spines.

question-5-6-hippopotamus.text: It has a huge round body and a very wide mouth, and rests in rivers.

question-5-6-horse.text: It is a hoofed animal with a flowing mane; our picture shows a plain brown coat.

question-5-6-house.text: It is a building where people can live.

question-5-6-jellyfish.text: It has a soft, jelly-like bell with tentacles hanging below it.

question-5-6-kangaroo.text: It has strong back legs for hopping, and the mother carries a baby in a pouch.

question-5-6-koala.text: It has fluffy round ears and a big dark nose, and rests in eucalyptus trees.

question-5-6-ladybug.text: It is a small round beetle; our picture shows red wing covers with black spots.

question-5-6-lion.text: It is a big wild cat with a mane.

question-5-6-lizard.text: It is a small reptile with dry scales, four legs, and a long tail.

question-5-6-monkey.text: It has grasping hands and a long tail, and it climbs trees.

question-5-6-moon.text: It looks like a crescent in this picture.

question-5-6-octopus.text: It is a soft sea animal with eight arms covered in suckers.

question-5-6-orange.text: It is a round fruit with an orange peel.

question-5-6-orange-color.text: It is the color of a carrot.

question-5-6-ostrich.text: It is a huge flightless bird with a long bare neck and powerful running legs.

question-5-6-otter.text: It is a slim, furry swimmer with whiskers, short legs, and a long tapering tail.

question-5-6-owl.text: It is a bird with large forward-facing eyes and a round face.

question-5-6-ox.text: It is a strong farm animal with hooves and horns, often used to pull a plow.

question-5-6-panda.text: It is a black-and-white bear that eats bamboo.

question-5-6-parrot.text: It is a colorful bird with a strong curved beak; some can copy human speech.

question-5-6-peacock.text: It is a bird that can spread long, eye-spotted feathers into a colorful fan.

question-5-6-pear.text: It is a green fruit with a narrow top and a wide bottom.

question-5-6-penguin.text: It is a black-and-white bird that swims with flippers instead of flying.

question-5-6-pig.text: It is a farm animal with a round snout that says oink.

question-5-6-polar-bear.text: It is a large white bear that lives near Arctic sea ice.

question-5-6-purple.text: It is the color of the grapes in our pictures.

question-5-6-rabbit.text: It has long ears and a little fluffy tail.

question-5-6-raccoon.text: It has a dark mask around its eyes and a tail with dark rings.

question-5-6-rat.text: It is a small rodent with a pointed nose and a long, nearly bare tail.

question-5-6-rectangle.text: This shape has two long sides and two short sides.

question-5-6-red.text: It is the color of a ripe strawberry.

question-5-6-rhinoceros.text: It is a heavy animal with thick skin and one or two horns on its nose.

question-5-6-rooster.text: It is a farm bird with a red comb that says cock-a-doodle-doo.

question-5-6-seahorse.text: It is a small upright fish with a horse-shaped head and a curled tail.

question-5-6-seal.text: It is a whiskered sea mammal with flippers and no outside ear flaps.

question-5-6-shark.text: It is a streamlined fish with gill slits and a pointed fin on its back.

question-5-6-snake.text: It has a long body covered in scales and no legs.

question-5-6-square.text: It has four equal straight sides and four corners.

question-5-6-squirrel.text: It is a small tree-climber with a bushy tail curled above its back.

question-5-6-starfish.text: It is a sea animal shaped like a star, often with five arms.

question-5-6-strawberry.text: It is a red fruit with tiny dots on the outside.

question-5-6-sun.text: It is the bright star that gives us daylight.

question-5-6-tiger.text: It is a big wild cat with orange fur and black stripes.

question-5-6-tree.text: It has a tall trunk and leafy branches.

question-5-6-triangle.text: It has three straight sides and three corners.

question-5-6-turtle.text: It has four legs and a hard shell.

question-5-6-whale.text: It is an enormous sea mammal with flippers and a broad tail that lies flat.

question-5-6-wolf.text: It is a wild, gray member of the dog family that howls.

question-5-6-woodpecker.text: It is a bird with a chisel-like bill that taps on tree trunks.

question-5-6-yellow.text: It is the color of a ripe banana peel.

question-5-6-zebra.text: It looks like a horse with black-and-white stripes.

question-7-8-ant.text: This narrow-waisted insect leaves scent trails to guide other members of its colony to food.

question-7-8-apple.text: This round, crunchy fruit has small seeds in a core.

question-7-8-banana.text: Peel its long yellow skin to find soft fruit inside.

question-7-8-bat.text: This is the only kind of mammal capable of true powered flight.

question-7-8-bear.text: This brown-furred bear has strong shoulder muscles that help it dig for food.

question-7-8-beaver.text: This flat-tailed rodent cuts branches with its teeth and can build dams.

question-7-8-bee.text: This fuzzy, striped insect carries pollen between flowers, and honey-making kinds live in hives.

question-7-8-blue.text: Mix this color with yellow paint to make green.

question-7-8-butterfly.text: This colorful-winged insect begins life as a caterpillar and changes inside a chrysalis.

question-7-8-camel.text: This desert traveler stores fat, not water, in its humps.

question-7-8-car.text: It carries people along roads on four wheels.

question-7-8-cat.text: This little pet has whiskers and can purr.

question-7-8-circle.text: This round shape has no straight sides and no corners.

question-7-8-crab.text: This clawed crustacean often walks sideways and sheds its shell as it grows.

question-7-8-crocodile.text: This long-jawed, toothy river reptile keeps its eyes and nostrils above water while most of its body stays hidden.

question-7-8-deer.text: The males of most kinds of this hoofed animal grow and shed branching antlers.

question-7-8-dog.text: This pet can bark and uses its strong sense of smell to explore.

question-7-8-dolphin.text: This beak-snouted sea mammal uses clicks and echoes to help locate fish.

question-7-8-dragon.text: This Chinese mythical creature appears in stories and festival dances; it is not a real animal.

question-7-8-duck.text: This quacking bird has webbed feet that work like paddles when it swims.

question-7-8-eagle.text: This white-headed, brown-winged bird of prey uses sharp eyesight to spot food from high above.

question-7-8-elephant.text: This animal uses its trunk to smell, drink, and pick things up.

question-7-8-flamingo.text: This long-legged water bird gets its pink color from pigments in its food.

question-7-8-flower.text: Its petals can help attract bees and butterflies.

question-7-8-fox.text: This orange member of the dog family can use its white-tipped bushy tail as a warm cover.

question-7-8-frog.text: This jumping amphibian begins life as a tadpole with a tail and no legs.

question-7-8-giraffe.text: This tallest living land animal uses its long neck to reach leaves high in trees.

question-7-8-goat.text: This bearded farm animal has split hooves that help it climb rocky slopes.

question-7-8-goose.text: Many wild relatives of this long-necked, honking farm bird migrate in a V-shaped flock.

question-7-8-gorilla.text: This largest living ape often walks on its knuckles and mainly eats plants.

question-7-8-grapes.text: These small, round fruits grow together on a vine.

question-7-8-green.text: Mix blue and yellow paint to make this color.

question-7-8-heart.text: Its two rounded top parts meet above a single bottom point.

question-7-8-hedgehog.text: This small spiny mammal can curl into a ball to protect its soft belly.

question-7-8-hippopotamus.text: This wide-mouthed river mammal spends much of the day in water and grazes on land at night.

question-7-8-horse.text: This domesticated animal has hooves and a long mane; its young are called foals.

question-7-8-house.text: This building has a roof, walls, and rooms for people to live in.

question-7-8-jellyfish.text: This bell-shaped sea animal has no brain, heart, or bones.

question-7-8-kangaroo.text: This Australian animal balances with its strong tail as it hops on large back legs.

question-7-8-koala.text: This Australian tree-dweller mainly eats eucalyptus leaves and is a marsupial, not a bear.

question-7-8-ladybug.text: Many kinds of this spotted beetle eat aphids that feed on garden plants.

question-7-8-lion.text: The male of this big wild cat often has a thick mane.

question-7-8-lizard.text: Some kinds of this small, four-legged, scaly reptile can drop their tails to escape danger.

question-7-8-monkey.text: Unlike an ape, this tree-climbing primate usually has a tail.

question-7-8-moon.text: It travels around Earth and reflects light from the Sun.

question-7-8-octopus.text: This eight-armed sea animal can squeeze through small gaps because it has no bones.

question-7-8-orange.text: Under its orange peel, this fruit separates into juicy sections.

question-7-8-orange-color.text: Mix red and yellow paint to make this color.

question-7-8-ostrich.text: This largest living bird has two toes on each foot and can run very fast.

question-7-8-otter.text: This sleek, long-tailed mammal has dense fur and uses its sensitive whiskers to help find prey in water.

question-7-8-owl.text: Many kinds of this round-faced bird hunt at night and fly very quietly.

question-7-8-ox.text: This animal is a trained working member of the cattle family.

question-7-8-panda.text: This black-and-white bear uses an extra wrist bone to help hold bamboo.

question-7-8-parrot.text: This curved-beaked bird has two toes pointing forward and two pointing backward on each foot.

question-7-8-peacock.text: The male of this bird displays a long train of colorful feathers to attract a mate.

question-7-8-pear.text: This fruit is wider at the bottom and narrower near its stem.

question-7-8-penguin.text: This flightless seabird uses its stiff, flat wings to move through the water.

question-7-8-pig.text: This snouted farm animal can roll in mud to help keep its body cool.

question-7-8-polar-bear.text: This Arctic bear has black skin beneath fur that looks white.

question-7-8-purple.text: Mix red and blue paint to make this color.

question-7-8-rabbit.text: This long-eared animal has strong back legs for hopping.

question-7-8-raccoon.text: This masked, ring-tailed mammal uses its sensitive front paws to explore food.

question-7-8-rat.text: This long-tailed rodent is the first animal in the Chinese zodiac.

question-7-8-rectangle.text: Its four corners are right angles, and it has two long sides and two short sides.

question-7-8-red.text: This is the color of the traffic light that tells cars to stop.

question-7-8-rhinoceros.text: The nose horns of this thick-skinned animal are made of keratin, like our fingernails.

question-7-8-rooster.text: This male chicken often crows to announce its presence.

question-7-8-seahorse.text: The father of this upright, curled-tail fish carries the eggs in a pouch.

question-7-8-seal.text: This flippered sea mammal rests on land or ice and uses whiskers to sense movement in water.

question-7-8-shark.text: This gill-breathing fish has a skeleton made of cartilage instead of bone.

question-7-8-snake.text: This legless reptile flicks its forked tongue to collect scent particles.

question-7-8-square.text: It has four equal sides, and every corner is a right angle.

question-7-8-squirrel.text: This bushy-tailed rodent often hides nuts in many places for later meals.

question-7-8-star.text: Its outline goes in and out to make five outer points.

question-7-8-starfish.text: This star-shaped sea animal moves using tiny tube feet underneath its arms.

question-7-8-strawberry.text: This red fruit has a leafy top and tiny seed-like dots on its skin.

question-7-8-sun.text: This star gives Earth light and warmth that help plants grow.

question-7-8-tiger.text: This large striped cat has a different stripe pattern on every individual.

question-7-8-tree.text: Its woody trunk supports branches, and its roots take in water.

question-7-8-triangle.text: Count its straight sides: there are exactly three.

question-7-8-turtle.text: This reptile has a shell that is part of its body.

question-7-8-whale.text: The blue kind of this enormous sea mammal is the largest animal alive today.

question-7-8-wolf.text: This wild dog relative howls to communicate with members of its pack.

question-7-8-woodpecker.text: This tree-tapping bird uses its stiff tail feathers to brace against a trunk.

question-7-8-yellow.text: This bright color is on a lemon peel and a ripe banana peel.

question-7-8-zebra.text: Every individual of this striped horse relative has a unique stripe pattern.
